sermon.title: Adding Love: How Did Jesus Love His Enemies?
sermon.series: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: The speaker asks how Jesus applied “love your enemies.” He shows Jesus walking through a synagogue mob (Luke 4), hiding from stoners (John 8:59), denouncing Pharisees (Matthew 23), calling Herod a fox (Luke 13), and not performing for Herod (Luke 23)—arguing that pattern is for non-criminal neighbors having a bad day, while maturity starts by changing yourself toward spouse and family.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Caption fixes: “dragged” for “drug,” “Herod/Herodias” for garbled “harry/harriet/heart be,” “them” for “him” where context is plural attackers. Sensitive: sharp language toward Pharisees/Hell; critique of healing-ministry showmanship; claim Jesus has no record of giving to the poor (priority is saving souls). Speaker not named in recording—confirm Kincer.
